يَرْفَئِىٌّ Heartless, or deprived of his heart, by reason of fright. (M, K.) ―
-b2- A male ostrich: (M:) or a male ostrich taking fright, and fleeing, or running away at random. (K.) ―
-b3- A gazelle; because of its briskness, liveliness, or sprightliness, and its uninterrupted running: (M:) or a gazelle that leaps, jumps, springs, or bounds, much, or often, (قَفُوزٌ,) and goes back, or retreats, (M, * K, TA,) fleeing. (TA.) ―
-b4- And A pastor of sheep or goats: (M, K:) it is said to have this meaning: (T:) or by this is meant a certain black slave so called. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
